name: Pudens
overview: Pudens is a male figure mentioned in the New Testament who is noted for sending greetings through the Apostle Paul to Timothy. Beyond this brief mention, Scripture provides no additional details about his tribal affiliation or personal background. His role is limited to this act of Christian fellowship and communication.
namesAndTitles: The name Pudens appears only once in Scripture and carries no specified meaning or divine origin in the biblical text. It is simply a proper name recorded in 2 Timothy 4:21 without further explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Pudens beyond the mention of his sending greetings via Paul to Timothy. There are no known relatives or connections detailed in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Pudens’ significance lies in his inclusion among the believers who maintained fellowship and encouraged one another during the early church period. His sending of greetings through Paul to Timothy highlights the personal and communal bonds among early Christians. Though a minor figure, he exemplifies the network of faithful believers supporting apostolic ministry.
